parties.note: Party of President Eduard Kokoity; won 20 of 34 seats in 2004 and 17 in 2009, none from 2014. The party infobox gives 2003 as the founding year, but the list of Prime Ministers already labels Gerasim Khugayev (from December 2001) as Unity Party. The 2026 election article calls Zurab Kokoyev its founder and longtime leader without dates, so he is recorded from 2026 only. Wikipedia lists nationalism and social conservatism (centre).
parties.review_note: Check the founding date (2003 in the infobox, but Unity-labelled Prime Ministers from 2001) and the leaders with dates (Kokoity, Bulatsev, Kokoyev).

parties.note: The party article says it was formed in the build-up to the May 2004 parliamentary election (no date given); 2004 is recorded. Won seats in every election from 2004. Leaders named in sources without person records here: Roland Kelekhsayev (chairman elected April 2009), Kazimir Pliyev (2009), Alexander Pliev (2014), Amiran Dyakonov (2019), Sergei Kharebov (2024, current per the party infobox). Wikipedia lists social liberalism (unsourced) and populism.

parties.note: Founded 5 September 2012; led by Anatoly Bibilov in the 2014 and 2019 elections; the party infobox now names Alan Tadtaev (no person record here; date of change not given). Wikipedia lists Russian conservatism, Ossetian nationalism and Russophilia.
parties.review_note: Bibilov is recorded as leader from the founding; check that and when Alan Tadtaev took over.

parties.note: Founded in 2013 by Alan Alborov (party infobox). Its list was led by Ruslan Gagloyev in 2014 (no birth date found, so no person record), David Sanakoev in 2019 and Zita Besayeva in 2024; Alan Gagloyev was its presidential candidate in 2022. Largest party in Parliament after 2024. Wikipedia lists Ossetian nationalism. Spelled Nykhaz in older articles.

parties.note: Founded in 2011; led by Vladimir Kelekhsaev (party infobox and the 2014 and 2019 election infoboxes; recorded from 2014). Won 6 seats in 2014 and 3 in 2019, none in 2024. Wikipedia lists Russophilia. Colour is a neutral placeholder.
